subject: Re: Redwood PoC trial plan & deployment mode (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood PoC recap & next steps (deployment mode and trial plan)

Hi Jordan / Sana —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get a PoC scoped and scheduled: 

Call recap
- Goal: validate Redwood for product recommendations pipeline (low latency generation + embeddings) and confirm cost/throughput for production traffic (peak ~200 qps internal simulation).
- Key constraints you mentioned: PHI in payloads for a subset of requests, EU data residency for reporting, procurement timeline aiming for decision by mid-June.

Deployment mode options (what we discussed)
1) Hosted API — fastest to start, no infra to manage, shared compute. Pros: lowest time-to-value; Cons: data residency & compliance restrictions may require additional controls.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools for Acme with predictable throughput and isolation. Pros: hits throughput/SLOs and cost predictability; Cons: longer lead time for reserved capacity allocation.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full network isolation and customer-managed environment. Pros: strongest data control for PHI; Cons: multi-week setup and additional ops overhead.

Proposed PoC / trial plan (high level)
- Success criteria (we recommend documenting):
  * Latency: p95 end-to-end generation < 250ms for 512-token prompt.
  * Throughput: sustained 100 qps with 200 qps burst handling in Dedicated mode.
  * Output quality: >= baseline BLEU/precision on your eval set (we'll use the sample prompt set from today).
  * Security: encrypted at rest + KMS integration for any PHI flows.
- Timeline: 4–6 weeks depending on deployment mode (Hosted = 1–2w, Dedicated = 3–6w, Private = 6–10w).
- Stakeholders: Jordan (Product), Sana (Platform/Security), Devon (Security) — please confirm availability for a kickoff.

Attachments: Redwood PoC template + Mutual Action Plan (attached).

Next steps
1) Jordan/Sana — confirm the preferred deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and any hard constraints (e.g., data residency, PHI that must remain in-county).
2) If Dedicated or Private, confirm required timeline and whether Procurement can sign a short-term reserved capacity commitment for the trial.
3) We'll draft a trial statement of work and a provisional quote and loop in Marissa (solutions/CS) to run the PoC operations.

I'm copying Marissa to start drafting the technical checklist and a proposed kickoff agenda. Happy to hop on a 15-min sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

1) Deployment mode leaning: Dedicated capacity looks like the right fit for the bulk of our workload given the latency and isolation needs. We still have a few PHI-sensitive flows that may need VPC controls; want to understand if Dedicated + KMS + regional hosting in us-east-1 would be sufficient.

2) Timeline: procurement prefers a 6-week runway to approve any reserved commitments; can we align the PoC to demonstrate the success criteria within that window?

3) Security items: attaching our security notes (high level) — main asks are SOC2 evidence, data residency in us-east-1, KMS/HSM support, and encryption at rest. Devon will own the detailed questionnaire.

Can you provide a provisional cost estimate for a 4-week Dedicated trial (reserved capacity) and sample SLA / uptime target? Also want to see a short PoC plan that outlines tasks we own vs Redwood owns.

Appreciate you and Marissa putting that together.

Hi Jordan / Sana —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing the security notes. I've sketched a short Dedicated-trial plan below that aligns with your 6-week procurement window and the success criteria Ben outlined.

Proposed Dedicated PoC plan (4 weeks inside a 6-week procurement window)
Week 0 (Kickoff) — Goal alignment, access provisioning, and test data checklist
- Deliverables: signed trial MOU / short-term reserved capacity agreement, PoC test dataset sanitized for PHI, IAM/KMS onboarding notes.
- Owners: Acme (test dataset, procurement), Redwood (provision reserved pool, KMS integration guide).

Week 1 (Integration)
- Deliverables: API connectivity, sample workload replay, baseline latency/throughput measurements.
- Owners: Acme infra (ingest), Redwood infra + CS (support).

Week 2 (Stress & QoE)
- Deliverables: sustained throughput load test to 100 qps, p95 latency reports, quality eval against provided eval set.
- Owners: joint runbook.

Week 3 (Tuning & Handover)
- Deliverables: configuration recommendations (batching, quantization profile), cost estimate for steady-state, knowledge transfer session.
- Owners: Redwood (ops + solutions), Acme (validation).

Success criteria
- p95 < 250ms for 512-token prompts under target load
- Sustained 100 qps with documented burst behavior to 200 qps
- Quality metrics meet or exceed baseline on the eval prompt set
- KMS integration validated for any PHI flows

Attachments: PoC checklist (see attached poc-checklist.docx). We'll also prepare a provisional quote and sample SLA; Ben will send the commercial docs.

Provisional asks for Acme to confirm ASAP
- Preferred start week (we can target kickoff the week of May 26)
- Primary security contact for questionnaire (Devon?)
- Any blocked IP ranges / networking constraints for Dedicated pool provisioning

I'll slot time for a 30-min kickoff once we have a preferred start date. Ben — if you can send the provisional quote and HubSpot link, I'll own the runbook and PoC coordination.

Thanks,
